message.content:
Take GitHub issue #77 ("Write the Devpost submission and the README's run instructions", lane:demo, P0, size:M, type:docs) in ehewes/durhack-proj from claim to a reviewed PR. The repo is Kip, a DurHack 2026 hackathon app about night noise and sleep, and speed matters. You run in your own isolated git worktree. Two other agents are working #70 (account) and #67 (works) in other worktrees at the same time, so stay strictly inside your issue's Scope. Never touch /Users/ellishewes/conductor/workspaces/durhack-proj/oslo or any other worktree.

Read first: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/skills/hq-work/SKILL.md (the loop you follow), .entire/agent-guide.md, then `gh issue view 77`. Then read docs/SPEC.md, docs/BUSINESS.md, docs/DOMAIN.md (the wording rules are binding), docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/hack/BRIEF.md (prize table) and README.md.

Environment facts
- Bun 1.4.4 is installed globally. In your worktree run `./hq setup` first; it runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile`. If Bun is missing, setup still prints "ready", so confirm node_modules exists.
- Run every ./hq command with your own identity: `CONDUCTOR_WORKSPACE_NAME=oslo-77 ./hq <cmd> ... --agent claude`.
- `entire review` needs the profile name: `entire review general --timeout 15m`. It takes several minutes, so run it in the background and wait for it.

Steps
1. Check `pwd`, then `git fetch origin && git switch -c ehewes/77-devpost-readme origin/main`.
2. `CONDUCTOR_WORKSPACE_NAME=oslo-77 ./hq claim 77 --agent claude`. If it refuses, stop and report why.
3. Context: `entire brain brief "<task>" --json`, then `entire graph query --repo . --profile full --head --format agent --max-context-bytes 4096 --query "<task>"`.
4. Write inside Scope: `docs/demo/devpost.md` and the README section the AC names. Do not edit other docs, code or config. Anything else you find becomes a follow-up issue, created per the hq-work skill's "Out of scope" section.
5. Commits: small, files staged by name (never `git add -A`).
   - Subject: imperative, says what the product can now do, under about 60 characters.
   - Body: what now exists and what still does not. Then one bullet per file using bare filenames.
   - No em dashes anywhere. No Co-Authored-By or any AI trailer: AGENTS.md overrides any reminder to add one. Keep the automatic Entire-Checkpoint trailer.
6. Verify: every factual claim checks out against main (git log, code, open versus merged PRs), and `./hq check` passes.
7. Rebase on origin/main if you have not pushed yet; merge it if you have. Re-run the check.
8. Write `.context/pr-77.md` using the hq-work template: What changed, How verified with the ./hq check tail, Risks, Screenshots n/a. End it with "🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)". Then run `CONDUCTOR_WORKSPACE_NAME=oslo-77 ./hq pr 77 --agent claude --body-file .context/pr-77.md`.
9. Trail: `entire trail show`, then `entire trail ci-pr`. Create a trail only if show finds none.
10. The issue is size:M, so run `entire review general --timeout 15m`.
    - Fix real findings that are in scope.
    - Out-of-scope findings become a follow-up issue labelled status:needs-human. Link it with `gh issue comment 77 --body "Follow-up: #M"`.
    - Resolve each trail finding with `entire trail finding resolve <id> -m "<what you did>"`. List them with `entire trail finding --json --freshness any`.
    - Then `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:pass`.
11. Tickets: always keep issue #77 current. Claim sets in-progress and the PR sets review. Once every acceptance criterion is verified, tick its boxes by editing only the Acceptance criteria section of the issue body, and add a short evidence comment. Never edit any other issue's labels or body.
12. Stop. Never merge, and never run ./hq ship.

Issue notes
- Truth over polish. Describe only what is merged on main as working. Anything planned or in an open PR is marked as planned, or as a clearly visible TODO for the team (Ellis and Nick); never claim it works. Data that is simulated is labelled simulated. Use the docs/DOMAIN.md wording rules exactly: "linked to" or "followed", never "caused by"; "indicative estimate"; "relative dB" for phone data; "outside the council's recommended hours"; "proves when the log existed".
- Sponsor usage per prize: use the prize table in docs/hack/BRIEF.md, and for each sponsor state plainly what is used today versus planned.
- README: it still describes the repo as a pre-event template with no product code. That is stale, because Kip is now built in this repo. Keep the pre-event tooling disclosure (MLH rule: only event work is judged; the hq framework was prepared before the event) and correct the intro. Add local run instructions that match the real package.json scripts and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (bun install, db:up, dev:api, dev:worker, dev:app, env vars from .env.example).
- Diagrams must be Mermaid code blocks. Keep it readable for judges skimming.

Final report (short): PR URL, branch and worktree path, ./hq check tail, review outcome and fixes, the TODOs left for the team, follow-up issues, and risks.

BRIEF.md
# DurHack 2026 agent framework (template)

A small framework for running many coding agents at once during a hackathon. Claude Code, Codex
and Cursor follow the same rules. GitHub Issues is the task queue, `./hq` is the CLI around it,
and [Entire](https://entire.com) records sessions, maps the codebase, keeps memory and runs reviews.

## Pre-event tooling disclosure
This repository is a template prepared before DurHack 2026. It holds tooling, agent rules, docs
and GitHub templates only: no product code. At kick-off we create a fresh submission repo from
this template (`gh repo create --template`). All product code is written during DurHack, in that
repo.

## Quickstart
- Humans: [docs/PLAYBOOK.md](docs/PLAYBOOK.md) (kick-off checklist, dispatching agents, onboarding).
- Agents: [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and the skills in [.agents/skills](.agents/skills).
- Hack context: [docs/hack/BRIEF.md](docs/hack/BRIEF.md), [docs/SPEC.md](docs/SPEC.md),
  [docs/BUSINESS.md](docs/BUSINESS.md), [docs/DOMAIN.md](docs/DOMAIN.md),
  [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), [docs/DECISIONS.md](docs/DECISIONS.md).
- First run in a clone: `entire enable`, then `./hq setup` (Windows: `hq.cmd setup`), then
  `./hq board`.

## Running the project
Kip is a Bun monorepo: an Expo app (`apps/mobile`, iOS and web), a Hono + tRPC server
(`apps/server`, API and worker) and shared domain code (`packages/shared`). Details in
[docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

```bash
bun install
cp .env.example .env        # local defaults; never commit .env
bun run db:up               # TimescaleDB + MongoDB in Docker
bun run dev:api             # http://localhost:3000; migrates on boot, skips any database not configured
bun run dev:worker          # cron jobs
bun run dev:app             # Expo: press w for web, or use a dev-client build on iPhone
./hq check                  # lint, typecheck, tests (what CI runs)
```

The iPhone app needs a dev-client build (`cd apps/mobile && bun run ios`) because of its native
modules; Expo Go won't load it. Deploy: `infra/` (Terraform) and the `Dockerfile`, see
[docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#deploy).

1	# Spec
2	
3	What we build. `/hq-plan` turns it into issues. Business detail is in `docs/BUSINESS.md`, the
4	science and wording rules in `docs/DOMAIN.md`.
5	
6	## Problem
7	The city measures night noise, but people feel it, and nobody connects the two. Newcastle's
8	Urban Observatory publishes kerbside noise levels and WHO publishes how night noise disturbs sleep,
9	yet a resident can't tell what woke them, and a traveller can't tell that a hotel overlooks a
10	24-hour demolition site. Bewick Court residents were kept awake until 5am by demolition under a
11	24-hour permit, and no open dataset recorded it.
12	
13	## Product
14	Kip shows how the city's noise affects sleep, street by street, and turns that into a Quiet Stay
15	Score for every hotel in Newcastle. It has three layers:
16	
17	| Layer | Feature | What the user sees |
18	|---|---|---|
19	| City | City sleep map | Each Observatory noise sensor shaded by an indicative % of nearby residents highly sleep disturbed |
20	| Personal | Personal night | Timeline of sleep stages, bedroom noise and wake-ups, each tagged with its likely cause |
21	| Personal | Morning briefing | Spoken summary on Watch or AirPods: "Two wake-ups followed drilling at 06:41, before the 8am limit" |
22	| Personal | Evidence log | An out-of-hours noise report for the council, its hash anchored on Solana |
23	| Business | Quiet Stays | Hotels ranked by predicted sleep quality for the traveller's profile, with booking links |
24	
25	City map and Personal night are the core; the rest build on them.
26	
27	## Users
28	- **Resident** near construction or nightlife: wants to know what wakes them and whether it broke
29	  the council's construction hours, with evidence they can send.
30	- **Traveller** choosing a Newcastle hotel: wants to know where they will sleep well, weighted for
31	  how they travel (light sleeper, night out, best value, business).
32	- **Judges**: see real city data, a real recorded night and one live noise event.
33	
34	## Demo script (3 min)
35	One live moment carries the pitch: a drilling sound hits the phone, and Kip labels it, checks the
36	council's hours and briefs you within seconds.
37	
38	| # | Time | Step | P |
39	|---|---|---|---|
40	| 1 | 0:00 | Hook: Bewick Court. "Where in Newcastle would you sleep worst tonight? Nobody can tell you. Kip can." | P0 |

1	# Domain
2	
3	The science, rules and wording Kip depends on. Code that computes, labels or displays any of
4	these must follow this file. Constants live in `packages/shared/src/domain/`, not inline.
5	
6	## Night noise and the WHO curve
7	- **Night window:** 23:00 to 07:00, `Europe/London` local time (handle BST changes).
8	- **Lnight:** the A-weighted equivalent level over the night window. It is an *energy* average,
9	  not an arithmetic mean of dB:
10	  `Lnight = 10 * log10(mean(10 ^ (L_i / 10)))`.
11	  In Tiger, average `power(10, db / 10)` and convert back with `10 * log10(...)`.
12	- **City estimate:** per sensor, the energy average of nightly Lnight over at least the last 30
13	  nights. Fewer than 30 nights: show the sensor as "not enough data", don't shade it.
14	- **WHO road-traffic curve** (Basner & McGuire 2018), % highly sleep disturbed:
15	  `%HSD = 19.4312 - 0.9336 * Lnight + 0.0126 * Lnight^2`.
16	  This reproduces the plan's figures (2.9% at 45 dB, 6.2% at 55 dB, 8.8% at 60 dB). Still check
17	  the paper before quoting more decimals.
18	- **Valid range:** 40 to 65 dB Lnight. Outside it, clamp for shading and mark the value as
19	  out of range; never extrapolate.
20	- **Thresholds** (WHO 2018): night-time road traffic below 45 dB Lnight, rail 44 dB, aircraft
21	  40 dB.
22	- **Limits:** the curve is for long-term road-traffic noise at a home's most exposed facade.
23	  Observatory sensors sit at the kerb and also pick up nightlife and voices. So the map is an
24	  *indicative road-traffic estimate*, never a measured disturbance rate.
25	
26	## Bedroom noise (phone)
27	- The iPhone microphone is not calibrated. Store and show **relative dB** only.
28	- Sample once a second. A **spike** is a level above the night's own baseline (rolling median)
29	  by a threshold set in `packages/shared`. Keep a 10-second clip around each spike.
30	- On-device voice-activity check: any clip containing speech is dropped on the phone and never
31	  uploaded.
32	
33	## Wake-up attribution
34	- **Wake-up signals:** a Watch "awake" stage during the sleep session, or a sudden heart-rate
35	  jump during sleep (Watch stages are coarse and miss brief arousals).
36	- **Method:** look for a spike in the 60 to 120 seconds before each wake-up, and compare the hit
37	  rate against randomly chosen windows of the same length from the same night.
38	- **Small numbers:** one night has 2 to 6 wake-ups. Show counts ("3 of 4 wake-ups followed a
39	  spike"). Show a percentage only once several nights are pooled from HealthKit history.
40	- HealthKit sleep stages appear only after the sleep session ends. Live demo mode needs no Watch
41	  data.
42	
43	## Noise classification
44	- Labels: `construction`, `traffic`, `siren`, `snoring`, `other`, plus `uncertain` and `handling`.
45	- **Handling noise** is the phone itself: rubbing on a sleeve, a pocket, a pillow or bedsheets.
46	  Kip's own small model (trained by us, see `ml/`) runs on each spike clip before Gemini. A clip
47	  that is mostly handling noise is labelled `handling`; otherwise the model's cleaned audio goes on
48	  to labelling. `handling` events are never linked to wake-ups and never appear in a briefing.
49	- Clips travel as 16 kHz mono 16-bit WAV, so the server needs no audio decoder.
50	- Gemini (paid-tier key) labels each clip, with JSON output. ElevenLabs Scribe audio-event tags
51	  give a second opinion. Where they disagree, the event is `uncertain`. This stops a user's own
52	  snoring being blamed on the building site.
53	- The clip is deleted once labelled. Only the label is kept.
54	
55	## Construction hours (Newcastle City Council)
56	Recommended hours for noisy construction work:
57	
58	| Day | Allowed |
59	|---|---|
60	| Monday to Friday | 08:00 to 18:00 |
61	| Saturday | 08:00 to 13:00 |
62	| Sunday and bank holidays | None |
63	
64	A `construction` event outside these hours is flagged "outside council hours". Bank holidays for
65	England come from `https://www.gov.uk/bank-holidays.json` (`england-and-wales`). These are
66	*recommended* hours: say "outside the council's recommended hours", not "illegal".
67	
68	## Street Manager
69	DfT Street Manager pushes street and road works permits in England (location, work category,
70	traffic management type, proposed and actual times) over AWS SNS to a public HTTPS endpoint. The
71	subscription must be confirmed within 3 days. It covers roads, not building or demolition sites.
72	Night work is inferred from proposed times and traffic management type.
73	
74	## Evidence log and Solana
75	Each night's log is serialised canonically, hashed (SHA-256), and the hash written to Solana
76	mainnet with the Memo program (no Anchor). It proves *when* a log existed, not that its contents
77	are true. Never claim more.
78	
79	## Wording rules
80	Anything user-facing, in the briefing prompt, the app (iOS or web) or the pitch:
81	
82	| Say | Never say |
83	|---|---|
84	| "linked to", "followed" | "caused by" |
85	| "indicative estimate" | "measured disturbance", "% of residents are disturbed" |
86	| "outside the council's recommended hours" | "illegal", "breach" |
87	| "relative dB" for phone data | bare "dB" for phone data |
88	| "simulated" on cohort data | anything implying simulated users are real |
89	| "proves when the log existed" | "proves the noise happened" |
90	
91	## Privacy (UK GDPR)
92	Sleep and heart data are special-category health data.
93	- Explicit, separate consent per data type: microphone, HealthKit, location.
94	- Store only relative dB, labelled events and HealthKit summaries. No raw audio at rest.
95	- Audio clips are deleted once labelled; clips with speech never leave the phone.
96	- One action deletes everything a user has, in both databases.
97	- Never log raw health values or audio in server logs.
98

1	# Business
2	
3	How Kip makes money and what the Quiet Stay Score is. Read this for any work on hotels, scoring,
4	profiles or booking links. Scoring maths and wording rules are in `docs/DOMAIN.md`.
5	
6	## Model
7	Kip recommends hotels on how well you'll sleep there and what's around them, and takes affiliate
8	commission on each booking. The same data that powers the city map and the personal night powers
9	the hotel ranking, so the business layer costs little extra to build.
10	
11	## Quiet Stay Score (0 to 100)
12	One score per hotel, built from data Kip already collects. It describes the hotel's surroundings,
13	not a specific room: the side of the building and the floor can matter as much as the street.
14	
15	| Input | Source | Effect on score |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| Indicative night-noise disturbance | Nearest Observatory noise sensors, distance-weighted, 30-night Lnight through the WHO road-traffic curve | Main factor |
18	| Active roadworks within 200 m | Street Manager permits; work scheduled at night (from proposed times and traffic management type) weighs more | Penalty for the dates of the stay only |
19	| Air quality at night | Observatory NO2 and PM2.5 | Small factor |
20	| Real nights nearby | Opted-in Kip users sleeping within 300 m | Corrects the estimate once there's enough data |
21	| Distance to nightlife and sights | OpenStreetMap venues | A preference, not a penalty (see profiles) |
22	
23	### Profiles
24	Kip asks one question up front and re-weights the score.
25	
26	| Profile | What Kip ranks first |
27	|---|---|
28	| Light sleeper | Lowest predicted disturbance |
29	| Night out | Within walking distance of nightlife, then quietest |
30	| Best value | Most quiet points per pound per night |
31	| Business | Quiet on weeknights, close to the station |
32	
33	### Rules for the score
34	- It is an estimate and the UI says so. Every score has its sources one tap away: which sensors,
35	  which permits, how many real nights. Without this, low-scoring hotels will dispute it.
36	- Weights live in one place, `packages/shared/src/domain/`, so the app can show the breakdown.
37	- Simulated cohort nights are flagged and labelled wherever they affect a score.
38	
39	## Revenue
40	1. **Affiliate commission (launch).** Booking links through affiliate networks. Booking.com cut
41	   thousands of smaller affiliates in 2025 and moved them to networks such as Awin and CJ;
42	   Expedia Group's affiliate programme and aggregators such as Travelpayouts are the other routes
43	   for a small team. Affiliate approval takes weeks, so the demo uses OpenStreetMap hotels with
44	   placeholder booking links. Don't quote a commission rate until it's confirmed.
45	2. **Verified Quiet (year one).** Hotels that already score well pay a yearly fee to replace the
46	   estimate with measured, room-by-room data from in-room sensors. Hotels that score badly get a
47	   free report showing which rooms and hours are the problem, as the route to a better score.
48	3. **Data licensing (later).** Area-level sleep disturbance data for councils, developers
49	   scheduling construction, and estate agents.
50	
51	## Hypotheses, not findings
52	- Renters choosing a flat for a 12-month lease may be a bigger market than hotel guests: same
53	  score, higher stakes. Pitch it as the next market, not as evidence.
54	
55	## Judge questions
56	| Question | Answer |
57	|---|---|
58	| Is this real data? | The city map, the recorded night and the permits are real; other users are simulated and labelled on the map |
59	| Does noise cause the wake-ups? | We claim a link, not a cause: wake-ups follow spikes more often than random moments do, shown as counts until there are enough nights for a percentage |
60	| Can you use the WHO curve on kerbside sensors? | Only as an indication: the curve is for long-term road-traffic noise, so we average 30 nights and label the map indicative |
61	| How accurate is a phone microphone? | Not calibrated, so Kip uses spikes above the night's own baseline in relative dB. The city estimate uses Observatory sensors, which were validated against precision meters |
62	| Do you record people's bedrooms? | Clips with speech are dropped on the phone; other clips are deleted once labelled. Health data needs explicit consent under UK GDPR, and users can delete everything |
63	| Why Solana? | Cheap public timestamps on mainnet that a council can check without trusting Kip. They prove when a log existed, not that it's true |
64	| Why two databases? | Timestamped numbers in Tiger, documents and geo queries in MongoDB |
65	| Why would hotels pay? | Well-scoring hotels pay to swap the estimate for measured, room-level data; low scorers get a free report on what to fix |
66	
67	## Sponsor mapping
68	All seven sponsors do real work in Kip. The prize table with targets is in `docs/hack/BRIEF.md`.
69	
70	| Sponsor | Role in Kip | What to show the judges | Fit |
71	|---|---|---|---|
72	| Vultr | Compute, Container Registry and firewall, all provisioned by Terraform | `terraform plan`, then `terraform apply -replace=vultr_instance.api` rebuilding the server while the data stays put | Strong |
73	| MongoDB Atlas | Users, night summaries, hotels and scores; geo queries | The hotel ranking pipeline: `$geoNear` on hotels, then `$geoWithin` lookups for nearby sensors and works | Strong |
74	| Gemini | Labels noise clips, writes the briefing and complaint draft, on a paid-tier key | Play a drilling clip and a siren clip; show the two labels | Strong |
75	| Tiger Data | All time-series data and the 30-night Lnight per sensor | The continuous aggregate that turns raw readings into the city map | Strong |
76	| ElevenLabs | Briefing voice, Scribe as a second classifier, Sound Effects for the demo clip | The briefing playing on AirPods, and the two classifiers agreeing | Medium to strong |
77	| Solana | Writes each night's log hash to mainnet with the Memo program | Edit a log on stage, re-hash it, show it no longer matches the on-chain memo | Medium |
78	| Entire | Records every agent session | One slide showing the recorded reasoning behind a key commit | Free win |

MongoDB holds one summary document per night plus users, 64 hotels, sensors, works and scores. 65 66 ## Stack 67 Bun is the package manager and workspace tool everywhere, and the server runtime. 68 69 | Layer | Choice | Notes | 70 |---|---|---| 71 | App | React Native + TypeScript on Expo (SDK current at kick-off) with a dev client, Expo Router, TanStack Query + tRPC client | One codebase, two targets: iOS (the phone on the nightstand) and web (the demo dashboard). Needs an Apple developer account and the HealthKit entitlement | 72 | HealthKit | `@kingstinct/react-native-healthkit` with its Expo config plugin | Reads the Watch's sleep stages, heart rate, HRV and respiratory rate after the night ends | 73 | Audio | Local Expo Module `kip-audio` (Swift): AVAudioRecorder metering at 1 Hz, 10 s spike clips, on-device speech check (SoundAnalysis built-in classifier), background audio mode | No JS library does all of this reliably while locked; one small native module does | 74 | Map | Web: Mapbox GL JS (`mapbox-gl`, style `light-v11`) in `Map.web.tsx`. iOS: MapLibre (`@maplibre/maplibre-react-native`) with OpenStreetMap raster tiles in `Map.native.tsx`. Both sit behind `lib/map`. Feature code passes GeoJSON points, lines and polygons, plus selection, clustering and camera changes, and does not import either SDK. | Public web token `EXPO_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_TOKEN`. Observatory, Street Manager and OpenStreetMap stay Kip's data sources. The basemap is only the canvas. | 75 | watchOS (stretch) | Native SwiftUI watch target: haptics, "something woke me", briefing playback | Only if Watch signing works in the first 2 hours | 76 | API | TypeScript, tRPC v11 on Hono (`@hono/trpc-server`), Zod, SuperJSON | tRPC for every JSON call and the live subscription (SSE). Plain Hono routes only for binary clip upload, the Street Manager SNS endpoint, health check and the web build | 77 | Worker | TypeScript, node-cron, same image as the API | Runs each feature's jobs | 78 | Time series | Tiger Data (TimescaleDB): hypertables plus continuous aggregates | Event-window and night-average queries | 79 | Documents | MongoDB Atlas with 2dsphere indexes | Hotel ranking is one aggregation pipeline | 80 | AI | Gemini API on a paid-tier key, JSON output | Free-tier keys aren't allowed for UK-facing apps | 81 | Voice | ElevenLabs TTS (briefing), Scribe (second classifier), Sound Effects (demo clip) | | 82 | Chain | Solana mainnet, Memo program only (no Anchor) | A memo costs a fraction of a penny | 83 | Hosting | Vultr Cloud Compute (London), Vultr Container Registry, Caddy with an `.sslip.io` hostname | iOS requires HTTPS; no domain needed | 84 | Infra | Terraform: `vultr/vultr`, `mongodb/mongodbatlas` (IP access list), Tiger Cloud provider; cloud-init via `templatefile()` | One command rebuilds the stack | 85 | Quality | Biome (lint + format), `tsc` per package (typecheck; not `tsc -b`, whose declaration checks reject the tRPC client types), `bun test` | `./hq check` runs all three; CI runs them plus Terraform and Docker builds | 86 | Process | Entire in the repo from the first commit | Records every agent session | 87 | ML | Python 3.11+, PyTorch, `uv`; trained on a Lium GPU pod; exported to ONNX and run in the API with ONNX Runtime | Our own small model that filters phone-handling noise out of spike clips. Not in `./hq check`: `ml/` runs `uv run pytest` | 88 89 `./hq check` runs the `check` commands in `hq.json`: `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, 90 `bun run test`. Keep it under ~2 min. `./hq setup` runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile`. 91 92 CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs on every PR and push to `main`, in three jobs: 93 `checks` (hq unit tests, then `./hq setup --ci` and `./hq check`), `terraform` (`fmt -check`, 94 `init -backend=false`, `validate` in `infra/`) and `docker` (builds the image, no push). 95 TypeScript is pinned to ~6.0.3, the version Expo SDK 58 expects. 96 97 ## File tree 98 The tree is split **by feature first, then by layer**, so several agents can build different 99 features at once without touching the same files. A feature is one product capability end to end: 100 its screens, its tRPC router, its business logic, its jobs, its schemas and its tests. 101 102 ``` 103 apps/ 104 mobile/ Expo app: iOS + web 105 app/ Expo Router routes. Thin: each file renders one feature screen 106 _layout.tsx providers (tRPC, query client), written in M0 107 (tabs)/_layout.tsx tab list, written in M0 with every tab stubbed 108 (tabs)/index.tsx -> features/city 109 (tabs)/night.tsx -> features/night 110 (tabs)/stays.tsx -> features/stays 111 live.tsx -> features/live 112 ... 113 src/ 114 features/ 115 / 116 screens/ full screens, imported by app/ 117 components/ feature-only components 118 hooks/ tRPC queries and mutations for this feature 119 native/ device APIs; platform files *.ios.ts / *.web.ts 120 index.ts the feature's public exports 121 lib/ 122 trpc.ts tRPC client, links, base URL 123 ui/ shared primitives (Button, Card, Text, theme) 124 map/ Map.native.tsx (MapLibre + OSM tiles), Map.web.tsx (Mapbox GL JS). 125 types.ts is the SDK-free interface. TypeScript resolves the native 126 file via `moduleSuffixes`; Metro picks per platform. 127 user-id.ts anonymous ID sent as `x-kip-user`, persisted on first launch 128 modules/ 129 kip-audio/ local Expo Module (Swift + TS bindings) 130 app.config.ts plugins, permission strings, background modes 131 server/ one package, one Docker image, two entrypoints 132 src/ 133 app.ts Hono app: /health, /trpc, each feature's plain routes, web build 134 main.api.ts connects, migrates, ensures indexes, serves app.ts 135 main.worker.ts registers every feature's jobs with node-cron 136 env.ts Zod-validated environment 137 trpc/ 138 init.ts initTRPC, context, procedures 139 router.ts appRouter: one line per feature router, written in M0 140 features/ 141 / 142 router.ts tRPC procedures. Thin: validate, call the service 143 service.ts business logic; the only thing other features may call 144 repo.ts this feature's Tiger and Mongo queries 145 jobs.ts optional cron jobs (`Job[]`), re-exported as `Jobs` 146 http.ts optional plain Hono routes (upload, SNS) 147 *.test.ts colocated tests 148 index.ts exports `Router`, `Jobs`, optional `Http`, 149 and the service functions others may use 150 integrations/ one client per external API: gemini.ts, elevenlabs.ts, 151 solana.ts, observatory.ts, overpass.ts, street-manager.ts 152 db/ 153 tiger.ts, mongo.ts clients; retry on boot 154 migrations/ SQL, one file per change, timestamp-prefixed; applied on API boot 155 migrate.ts migration runner (`bun run db:migrate`); checks TimescaleDB is installed 156 indexes.ts Mongo collections and indexes 157 packages/ 158 shared/ pure TypeScript, no IO; used by app and server 159 src/ 160 / Zod schemas and types for that feature's inputs and outputs 161 domain/ WHO curve, Lnight, construction hours, attribution maths, 162 score weights, wording strings, each with tests 163 infra/ Terraform, cloud-init.yaml.tftpl (writes the Caddyfile and compose) 164 compose.yaml local TimescaleDB and MongoDB for development 165 ml/ handling-noise filter: data scripts, model, training, ONNX export (Python, uv) 166 audio/ committed audio library, 16 kHz mono WAV: ours/, online/, synthetic/, generated/ (licences in SOURCES.md) 167 models/handling-v1.onnx the exported model the API loads (small, committed) 168 Dockerfile builds server + Expo web export into one image 169 ``` 170 171 The app gets end-to-end types from `import type { AppRouter } from "@kip/server/trpc/router"`. 172 It never imports server runtime code. 173 174 ### Features 175 | Feature | App (`apps/mobile/src/features/`) | Server (`apps/server/src/features/`) | Its data | 176 |---|---|---|---| 177 | `city` | City map screen | Sensors query, Observatory ingest job | 30-night Lnight and %HSD per sensor | 178 | `night` | Recording, upload, night timeline | Night upload, timeline query | Night documents and noise samples | 179 | `attribution` | Wake-up markers and counts on the timeline | Wake-up detection, spike vs random-window counts | Attribution results on a night | 180 | `labels` | Label chips on events | Clip upload route, Gemini + Scribe labelling, clip deletion | Event labels, `uncertain` logic | 181 | `briefing` | Briefing player | Gemini narrative, ElevenLabs TTS | Briefing text and audio | 182 | `evidence` | Evidence log, council report, verify view | Log hashing, Solana memo, complaint draft | Hashes, memo signatures | 183 | `stays` | Quiet Stays list, profile picker, score breakdown | Hotel ranking pipeline, OSM hotels and venues job | Hotels, venues, scores | 184 | `works` | Works layer on the map | Street Manager SNS route, permit storage | Works documents | 185 | `live` | Live demo screen (iOS sender, web viewer) | Live sample mutation and subscription | Live session state (in memory) | 186 | `account` | Onboarding, consent, delete everything | User, consent, profile, cascade delete | Users | 187 188 Construction-hours checks and the WHO curve live in `packages/shared/src/domain/`, since several 189 features and both apps use them. 190 191 ### Rules that keep parallel agents apart 192 1. **Stay in your feature.** An issue names one feature. Its agent edits only that feature's 193 folders in `apps/mobile`, `apps/server` and `packages/shared`, plus a new migration file. 194 2. **No reaching into another feature.** Import another feature only through its `index.ts`, and 195 only service functions it exports. Never import its `repo.ts`, components or hooks. Need more 196 from it? Open an issue for that feature. 197 3. **Registries are written once, in M0.** `trpc/router.ts`, `main.worker.ts`, 198 `app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx` and the routes in `app/` are created with every feature stubbed, so 199 feature work never edits them. Adding a feature later is its own issue. 200 4. **Shared code changes through its own issue:** `lib/ui`, `lib/map`, `trpc/init.ts`, 201 `integrations/`, `db/` clients, `packages/shared/src/domain/`, `modules/kip-audio`, 202 `app.config.ts`. Adding a new file in `integrations/` is fine; changing an existing one is not. 203 5. **Conflict-free by construction:** migrations are named 204 `YYYYMMDDHHMM__.sql`; `env.ts` and `.env.example` take one line per variable, 205 grouped by feature; never hand-merge `bun.lock`, rerun `bun install` instead. 206 6. **Platform splits by filename**, not `if (Platform.OS)` branches: `foo.ios.ts` and `foo.web.ts`. 207 iOS-only features (recording, HealthKit) ship a `.web.ts` stub that renders "Open on iPhone". 208 209 ## Lanes 210 Lanes are features. Both of us own every lane; lanes only exist so parallel issues touch 211 disjoint paths. Each lane covers that feature's folder in `apps/mobile/src/features/`, 212 `apps/server/src/features/` and `packages/shared/src/`. They are mirrored in `hq.json`. 213 214 | Lane | Dirs | 215 |---|---| 216 | `city`, `night`, `attribution`, `labels`, `briefing`, `evidence`, `stays`, `works`, `live`, `account` | `*/features//`, `packages/shared/src//` | 217 | `platform` | `apps/mobile/app/`, `apps/mobile/src/lib/`, `apps/mobile/modules/`, `apps/mobile/app.config.ts`, `apps/server/src/*.ts` (`app.ts`, `main.*.ts`, `env.ts`, `jobs.ts`, `http.ts`, `retry.ts`), `apps/server/src/{trpc,integrations,db}/`, `packages/shared/src/domain/`, root config (`package.json`, `biome.json`, `tsconfig.base.json`, `compose.yaml`), `.github/workflows/` | 218 | `infra` | `infra/`, `Dockerfile` | 219 | `demo` | `docs/demo/` (pitch, Devpost, demo clips, Entire evidence) | 220 | `ml` | `ml/` (Python: data, training, export; raw data and checkpoints stay out of git) | 221 222 ## Contracts 223 Merge in M0, before anyone branches. Agree the night upload schema in the first 30 minutes so 224 recording and server work never block each other. 225 226 | Contract | Lives in | Lane | 227 |---|---|---| 228 | Night upload schema | `packages/shared/src/night/upload.ts` | `night` | 229 | Each feature's tRPC inputs and outputs | `packages/shared/src//`, used by `features//router.ts` | that feature | 230 | tRPC context, procedures, root router | `apps/server/src/trpc/` | `platform` | 231 | Domain constants (night window, spike threshold, attribution window, construction hours, WHO curve, score weights) | `packages/shared/src/domain/` | `platform` | 232 | `kip-audio` JS API | `apps/mobile/modules/kip-audio/index.ts` | `platform` | 233 | Tiger schema | `apps/server/src/db/migrations/` | the feature in the file name | 234 | Mongo collections and indexes | `apps/server/src/db/indexes.ts` | `platform` | 235 | Handling-filter model I/O: 16 kHz mono float32 PCM in; cleaned PCM and a per-frame handling probability out | `ml/README.md`, `ml/models/` | `ml` | 236 | Spike clip format: 16 kHz mono 16-bit WAV | `apps/mobile/modules/kip-audio/index.ts` | `platform` | 237 238 ### Night upload (draft, settle at M0) 239 ```ts 240 NightUpload = z.object({ 241 nightId: z.string().uuid(), userId: z.string().uuid(), 242 startedAt: z.string().datetime({ offset: true }), // Europe/London offsets 243 endedAt: z.string().datetime({ offset: true }), 244 location: z.object({ lat: z.number(), lon: z.number() }).optional(), // location consent only 245 consent: z.object({ microphone: z.boolean(), health: z.boolean(), location: z.boolean() }), 246 noise: z.object({ baselineDb: z.number(), samples: z.array(z.tuple([z.number(), z.number()])) }), // [epochSec, relative dB], 1 Hz 247 spikes: z.array(z.object({ t: z.number(), peakDb: z.number(), clipId: z.string().optional() })), 248 sleep: z.object({ // absent in live demo mode 249 stages: z.array(z.object({ start: z.string(), end: z.string(), 250 stage: z.enum(["inBed", "awake", "core", "deep", "rem"]) })), 251 heartRate: z.array(z.tuple([z.number(), z.number()])), 252 hrv: z.array(z.tuple([z.number(), z.number()])), 253 respiratoryRate: z.array(z.tuple([z.number(), z.number()])), 254 }).optional(), 255 }) 256 ``` 257 258 ### tRPC routers (draft) 259 | Router | Procedures | 260 |---|---| 261 | `night` | `upload` (mutation), `get`, `list` | 262 | `labels` | `forNight`; clip bytes go to plain `POST /upload/clip`, which labels and then deletes them | 263 | `attribution` | `forNight` | 264 | `briefing` | `get` (text and audio URL) | 265 | `evidence` | `anchor` (mutation), `verify`, `report` | 266 | `live` | `push` (mutation), `stream` (subscription over SSE) | 267 | `city` | `sensors` | 268 | `stays` | `rank({ profile, checkIn, checkOut, near? })` | 269 | `works` | `near`; permits arrive on plain `POST /sns/street-manager` | 270 | `account` | `me`, `setConsent`, `setProfile`, `deleteEverything` | 271 272 Auth for the hackathon: the app generates a user ID on first launch and sends it as a header; 273 `trpc/init.ts` puts it on the context. No accounts or passwords. 274 275 ## Data 276 ### Tiger (TimescaleDB) 277 | Table | Kind | Key columns | Feature | 278 |---|---|---|---| 279 | `sensor_readings` | hypertable | `time, sensor_id, metric (noise_db, no2, pm25), value` | `city` | 280 | `sensor_lnight_daily` | continuous aggregate | Energy-averaged noise per sensor per night window (see `docs/DOMAIN.md`) | `city` | 281 | `night_noise` | hypertable | `time, night_id, db` (relative) | `night` | 282 | `sleep_stages` | table | `night_id, start, end, stage` | `night` | 283 | `vitals` | hypertable | `time, night_id, metric (hr, hrv, resp), value` | `night` | 284 285 The 30-night Lnight per sensor is a query over `sensor_lnight_daily`. Backfill at least 30 nights 286 of Observatory history in hour one. 287 288 ### MongoDB Atlas 289 | Collection | Holds | Indexes | Feature | 290 |---|---|---|---| 291 | `users` | Consent, profile choice | | `account` | 292 | `nights` | One summary per night: events, labels, attribution counts, hours flags, log hash, memo signature | `userId, startedAt` | `night` (others add fields through its service) | 293 | `sensors` | Observatory sensor, GeoJSON point, latest 30-night Lnight and %HSD | `2dsphere` | `city` | 294 | `hotels` | OSM hotel, GeoJSON point, placeholder booking link, `simulated` flags | `2dsphere` | `stays` | 295 | `venues` | OSM nightlife and sights | `2dsphere` | `stays` | 296 | `works` | Street Manager permits, geometry, proposed/actual times, night flag | `2dsphere` | `works` | 297 298 Hotel ranking is one pipeline: `$geoNear` on `hotels` first (only one is allowed, and it must be 299 the first stage), then `$lookup` with `$geoWithin` and `$centerSphere` into `sensors`, `works` and 300 `venues`, then the profile weights from `packages/shared/src/domain/`. 301 302 ## Env vars 303 Secrets live in `.env`, never committed and never pasted into a prompt. Not a secret | 315 | `EXPO_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_TOKEN` | App, web map | Mapbox public token (`pk.`). Restrict it to the dashboard origins. Not a secret. Never commit a real token. iOS does not read it | 316 | `VULTR_API_KEY` | Terraform | Vultr account (MLH credit) | 317 | `MONGODB_ATLAS_PUBLIC_KEY`, `MONGODB_ATLAS_PRIVATE_KEY` | Terraform | Atlas org API key | 318 | Tiger Cloud provider credentials | Terraform | Tiger Cloud console; names per the provider docs | 319 | `TF_VAR_admin_ip`, `TF_VAR_image`, `TF_VAR_registry_user`, `TF_VAR_registry_password`, `TF_VAR_mongo_uri`, `TF_VAR_tiger_uri`, `TF_VAR_app_env` | Terraform | See `infra/terraform.tfvars.example`; `app_env` carries the API keys above to the server | 320 321 Only `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` variables reach the app, and they end up in the bundle: never put a secret 322 key there. `EXPO_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_TOKEN` is a public `pk.` token, not a secret. 323 324 ## Deploy 325 Either of us deploys. The demo runs from tag `demo-v1`. 326 - `infra/` holds Terraform: SSH key, private container registry, firewall (22 from `admin_ip` 327 only; 80 and 443 open for Caddy), a `vc2-2c-4gb` Ubuntu 24.04 instance in `lhr`, and the Atlas IP 328 access list for the instance's IP. Keys come from variables, never the repo. 329 - The `Dockerfile` builds the server and `expo export --platform web` into one image; the API 330 serves the web build on port 8080 (`docker run -p 8080:8080 kip`). Without database URIs it 331 still boots, serving `/health`, the web build and the stubs. Steps: `infra/README.md`. 332 - cloud-init installs Docker, writes `/opt/kip/.env`, a Caddyfile and a compose file, derives an 333 `.sslip.io` hostname from instance metadata, logs in to the registry, then runs the API, 334 the worker (same image, `main.worker.ts`) and Caddy. 335 - Ship a new image: `docker build -t . && docker push `, then on the server 336 `cd /opt/kip && docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`. 337 - The API retries its database connections on boot, because the Atlas access list is applied 338 after the instance exists. The image reference and registry credentials are variables, so nothing depends on the 343 registry's `urn` attribute. 344

=== .env.example
# Copy to .env. Secrets never go in the repo or an agent prompt (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, "Env vars").
# Every variable is optional in development; production needs MONGO_URI and TIGER_URI.
# One line per variable, grouped by feature.

# platform: local databases from `bun run db:up`
PORT=3000
MONGO_URI=mongodb://localhost:27017/kip
TIGER_URI=REDACTED
WEB_DIST=

# labels, briefing: Gemini (paid tier, billing enabled)
GEMINI_API_KEY=
# labels, briefing: ElevenLabs
ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=

# evidence: Solana mainnet, a small funded keypair used only for memos
SOLANA_RPC_URL=
SOLANA_KEYPAIR=

# works: Street Manager open data over SNS
STREET_MANAGER_TOPIC_ARN=

# app: where the iPhone or Expo web dev server finds the API. Use your Mac's LAN IP for a phone.
EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:3000

# app: Mapbox public token (pk.) for the web map. Restrict it to the dashboard origins.
# iOS still uses MapLibre. Never commit a real token.
EXPO_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_TOKEN=

# infra (Terraform only, not read by the app): see infra/terraform.tfvars.example
VULTR_API_KEY=
MONGODB_ATLAS_PUBLIC_KEY=
MONGODB_ATLAS_PRIVATE_KEY=
TF_VAR_admin_ip=
=== compose.yaml
# Local development databases. Production uses Tiger Cloud and MongoDB Atlas.
services:
  tiger:
    image: timescale/timescaledb:latest-pg17
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: REDACTED
      POSTGRES_DB: kip
    ports: ["5432:5432"]
    volumes: [tiger:/var/lib/REDACTEDql/data]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "pg_isready", "-U", "REDACTED"]
      interval: 2s
      retries: 30

  mongo:
    image: mongo:8
    ports: ["27017:27017"]
    volumes: [mongo:/data/db]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "mongosh", "--quiet", "--eval", "db.runCommand({ ping: 1 })"]
      interval: 2s
      retries: 30

volumes:
  tiger:
  mongo:

content.content:
1	# Decisions
2	
3	Append-only log, newest at the bottom. Add an entry when a choice would surprise a newcomer or is
4	costly to undo. Agents also record it with `entire brain remember "<decision>"`.
5	
6	Format:
7	
8	```
9	## YYYY-MM-DD: <decision>
10	**Context:** why it came up.
11	**Decision:** what we chose.
12	**Consequences:** what follows, good and bad.
13	```
14	
15	## 2026-11-13: GitHub Issues is the single task queue
16	**Context:** Up to ~10 agents across Claude Code, Codex and Cursor need one shared view of the
17	work. A second tracker (beads, Backlog.md, Task Master) would drift from GitHub.
18	**Decision:** Every task is a GitHub issue in the task form. `./hq` claims, labels and ships them.
19	Humans dispatch; agents never pick their own.
20	**Consequences:** GitHub is the only shared state; `.context/` and workspaces are scratch. Every
21	agent needs `gh` auth and network access.
22	
23	## 2026-11-13: Entire for sessions, memory and review
24	**Context:** We want shared session history, codebase mapping, persistent memory and cross-vendor
25	review, and we target Best Use of Entire. Entire's judging tool only reads `refs/heads/entire/*`.
26	**Decision:** Use Entire Sessions, Graph, Brain and Trails, and `entire review` (Claude Code and
27	Codex reviewers, one judge). Use the `branch` checkpoint backend.
28	**Consequences:** Every session is recorded and pushed, so no secrets in prompts. Each clone runs
29	`entire enable`. `review:pass` needs local `entire review`, hosted Trail review or `/hq-review`.
30	
31	## 2026-11-13: Squash merges keep Entire-Checkpoint trailers
32	**Context:** Entire links commits to sessions through `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers. A squash
33	message without them breaks the link.
34	**Decision:** Squash merge only. Repo setting: squash title = PR title, message = commit details.
35	`./hq ship` merges this way.
36	**Consequences:** `main` gets one commit per PR and `entire why` still resolves to sessions. Never
37	edit the trailers out of a squash message.
38	
39	## 2026-11-13: Fresh submission repo from this template at kick-off
40	**Context:** MLH only judges work done during the event, and Entire's judging tool scores a clean
41	start higher.
42	**Decision:** This repo is a template. At kick-off we run `gh repo create --template` and hack in
43	the new repo.
44	**Consequences:** The submission has no pre-event history. Pre-kick-off agent sessions are closed
45	and fresh ones started. The README discloses the framework as pre-event tooling.
46	
47	## 2026-11-14: Kip is the project
48	**Context:** The plan "Kip: Sleep, Noise and the City" (Nick, 2026-11-14) covers product, business
49	model, stack, build plan and pitch.
50	**Decision:** Build Kip. Product in `docs/SPEC.md`, business in `docs/BUSINESS.md`, science and
51	wording rules in `docs/DOMAIN.md`, stack and contracts in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
52	**Consequences:** Every agent follows `docs/DOMAIN.md` for anything it computes or shows.
53	
54	## 2026-11-14: The API is the only caller of third-party services
55	**Context:** Gemini, ElevenLabs and Solana need secret keys; the app (iOS and web) is a client.
56	**Decision:** Only the API calls Gemini, ElevenLabs and Solana. Clients call the API.
57	**Consequences:** Keys live in one place. Clip labelling and briefings need a network round trip.
58	
59	## 2026-11-14: Tiger for time series, MongoDB for documents and geo
60	**Context:** Kip has dense timestamped data (1 Hz noise, sensor readings, vitals) and geo
61	documents (hotels, sensors, works). Both are sponsor tracks.
62	**Decision:** Every timestamped value goes in Tiger; MongoDB holds users, one summary per night,
63	hotels, sensors, works, venues and scores. If the event limits us to one sponsor track, enter
64	MongoDB: move the time series into MongoDB time series collections and make hotel ranking the
65	centrepiece.
66	**Consequences:** Two stores to provision and delete from. User deletion must cover both.
67	
68	## 2026-11-14: Read Watch data through HealthKit, not a Watch app
69	**Context:** An all-night workout session drains 40% to 100% of a Watch battery, and Watch app
70	signing is a known time sink.
71	**Decision:** The iPhone reads the Watch's own sleep tracking from HealthKit after the night ends.
72	A watchOS app is a stretch, abandoned if signing doesn't work by hour 2.
73	**Consequences:** Sleep stages arrive only after the session ends, so the live demo uses the
74	phone alone.
75	
76	## 2026-11-14: Claim links, not causes; label estimates
77	**Context:** One night has 2 to 6 wake-ups, phone dB is uncalibrated, and the WHO curve is for
78	long-term road traffic at the facade, not kerbside sensors.
79	**Decision:** Show counts against a random-window baseline, relative dB, and an "indicative" city
80	map. Follow the wording table in `docs/DOMAIN.md`.
81	**Consequences:** Weaker-sounding claims that survive judge questions.
82	
83	## 2026-11-14: Placeholder booking links for the demo
84	**Context:** Affiliate approval takes weeks; Booking.com cut small affiliates in 2025.
85	**Decision:** Hotels come from OpenStreetMap with placeholder booking links. Apply to a network
86	anyway and don't quote a commission rate until confirmed.
87	**Consequences:** Revenue is shown as the model, not as live bookings.
88	
89	## 2026-11-14: Solana mainnet with the Memo program only
90	**Context:** We want cheap public timestamps a council can check without trusting Kip.
91	**Decision:** Hash each night's log and write it to mainnet with the Memo program. No Anchor, no
92	custom program.
93	**Consequences:** No toolchain setup; a fraction of a penny per night. It proves when a log
94	existed, not that it's true, and we say so.
95	
96	## 2026-11-14: Bun workspaces; one server package and image
97	**Context:** The API and worker share clients, schemas and database code, and the plan wants one
98	Docker image.
99	**Decision:** Bun is the package manager for the whole repo and the server runtime.
100	`apps/server` holds both entrypoints (`main.api.ts`, `main.worker.ts`) and builds with the Expo
101	web export into one image.
102	**Consequences:** One build and deploy, one lockfile. Never hand-merge `bun.lock`.
103	
104	## 2026-11-14: React Native on Expo for both the phone and the dashboard
105	**Context:** The team's strongest language is TypeScript, and the demo needs an iPhone app and a
106	browser dashboard.
107	**Decision:** One Expo app (dev client, Expo Router) builds iOS and web. HealthKit through
108	`@kingstinct/react-native-healthkit`; background metering, spike clips and the speech check in a
109	small local Expo Module (`kip-audio`, Swift). Replaces the plan's SwiftUI app and React/Vite
110	dashboard.
111	**Consequences:** One UI codebase and shared types. The native audio module is the riskiest
112	piece: build and test it on a device first. Maps need a `.native`/`.web` split. A watchOS app
113	becomes a separate native target, so it stays a stretch.
114	
115	## 2026-11-14: tRPC on Hono for the API
116	**Context:** App and server are both TypeScript, and several agents change API shapes in parallel.
117	**Decision:** tRPC v11 mounted on Hono. Every JSON call and the live subscription go through
118	tRPC; plain Hono routes only for binary clip upload, the Street Manager SNS endpoint, health and
119	the web build.
120	**Consequences:** End-to-end types with no codegen; a server change that breaks the app fails
121	typecheck. Non-TypeScript clients (SNS) still get plain HTTP.
122	
123	## 2026-11-14: File tree by feature, then by layer
124	**Context:** Up to ~10 agents work at once. A layer-first tree (`routes/`, `services/`,
125	`screens/`) puts every task in the same folders.
126	**Decision:** Each feature (`city`, `night`, `attribution`, `labels`, `briefing`, `evidence`,
127	`stays`, `works`, `live`, `account`) owns a folder in `apps/mobile/src/features/`,
128	`apps/server/src/features/` and `packages/shared/src/`. Lanes are features. Registries are
129	written once in M0 with every feature stubbed; shared code changes through `platform` issues.
130	**Consequences:** Parallel issues touch disjoint paths. Cross-feature calls go through a feature's
131	`index.ts`. The rules are in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
132	
133	## 2026-11-14: Both of us own everything
134	**Context:** The template gave Ellis `main`, deploys and the freeze, and gave each human lanes.
135	With two people working across the whole stack, that split only adds hand-offs.
136	**Decision:** No split ownership. Either of us can merge any PR, deploy, call the freeze and tag
137	`demo-v1`. Lanes stay, but only to keep parallel agents on disjoint paths.
138	**Consequences:** No waiting on a specific person. Say in chat before merging contracts, deploy
139	config or anything after the freeze, so we don't both do it.
140	
141	## 2026-11-14: Train our own handling-noise filter on a Lium GPU pod
142	**Context:** A phone on a nightstand, in a pocket or under a pillow picks up its own handling noise
143	(sleeve, pocket, bedsheet rustle). Those spikes would be labelled and linked to wake-ups. We also
144	want a model of our own in the pipeline, not only third-party APIs.
145	**Decision:** Train a small PyTorch mask model on synthetic mixtures of handling noise and night
146	sounds, on a Lium GPU pod (Vultr stays for deployment). Export it to ONNX and run it in the API on
147	each spike clip before Gemini. Mostly-handling clips get the label `handling`. Clips are 16 kHz mono
148	WAV. Prototype quality is acceptable: if the model underperforms, the API falls back to labelling
149	the original clip.
150	**Consequences:** A Python toolchain (`uv`) beside Bun, outside `./hq check`. Training data and
151	checkpoints stay out of git; only the exported model is committed. The label set gains `handling`,
152	which attribution and briefings ignore.
153	
154	## 2026-11-14: Commit a small curated audio library in `ml/audio/`
155	**Context:** Both of us, and agents on any machine or a Lium pod, need the same recordings and
156	downloaded clips, and Ellis wants to upload recordings straight into the repo.
157	**Decision:** `ml/audio/` holds our recordings, ESC-50 background clips, placeholder synthetic
158	handling noise and ElevenLabs-generated clips, all 16 kHz mono WAV with sources in
159	`ml/audio/SOURCES.md`, committed to git. Keep it small (tens of MB): short takes only. Generated
160	mixtures, runs and checkpoints still stay out of git. No Git LFS, because its hooks clash with
161	Entire's.
162	**Consequences:** Every clone carries the audio library. ESC-50 is CC BY-NC, acceptable for the
163	prototype only. Raw Voice Memos files stay in the ignored `ml/audio/inbox/`.
164	
165	## 2026-11-14: Recordings with other people's conversation stay out of git
166	**Context:** The venue is loud. The room tone and the Watch's general audio are mostly other attendees
167	talking, and the repo becomes public at submission.
168	**Decision:** Every recording is scanned with Apple's sound classifier. Speech windows (confidence 0.5
169	or more) are cut from committed clips; recordings that are mostly conversation go to the git-ignored
170	`ml/audio/private/`, used for training on our machines or the Lium pod only, and deleted after the event.
171	**Consequences:** The committed handling set is smaller (about 3 minutes). The data pipeline must cope
172	with room tone being absent on a fresh clone, for example by taking the noise floor from each take's
173	quiet start and end.
174	
175	## 2026-11-14: Web maps use Mapbox GL JS
176	**Context:** The web dashboard needs a basemap that stays readable under city, works and stay
177	layers, with selection, clustering and camera changes. The first shell used MapLibre and
178	OpenStreetMap raster tiles on both web and iOS.
179	**Decision:** `Map.web.tsx` renders with Mapbox GL JS and the restrained `light-v11` style. The
180	public token comes from `EXPO_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_TOKEN` (a `pk.` token, URL-restricted in the Mapbox
181	console, never committed). Feature code draws GeoJSON points, lines and polygons through `lib/map`
182	and does not import Mapbox or MapLibre. iOS stays on MapLibre with OpenStreetMap raster tiles until
183	a native Mapbox migration. Observatory, Street Manager and OpenStreetMap remain Kip's data sources;
184	the basemap is only the canvas. The map does not request device location to show Newcastle, and
185	Mapbox attribution stays visible.
186	**Consequences:** The web export shows Newcastle tiles only when the public token is set. A missing
187	token shows a message naming `EXPO_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_TOKEN` instead of a blank map. The phone build does
188	not gain a Mapbox native SDK. Secret Mapbox tokens (`sk.`) stay out of the app.
189

content.content:
# ml: Kip's handling-noise filter

Our own small model that removes phone-handling noise (sleeve, pocket, pillow, bedsheet rustle) from
spike clips before Gemini labels them. Plan and contracts: `docs/DOMAIN.md` (Noise
classification), `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (ML row, `ml` lane), `docs/DECISIONS.md`. Issues: #85 to #92.

## See it
**[MODEL.md](MODEL.md)**: how the model works, the theory behind it, and how it is measured.

**[notebooks/handling_poc.ipynb](notebooks/handling_poc.ipynb)**: the data, training curves, comparison with a
spectral noise gate, waveforms and spectrograms before and after, and real phone takes. GitHub renders it with every
chart; to play the audio and run it yourself: `uv sync --group dev && uv run jupyter lab notebooks/handling_poc.ipynb`.

## Results so far
The exported model (`models/handling-poc.onnx`) is the RTX 3090 run: 0.42M parameters, 15,000 steps, trained on a Lium
pod for $0.16. On held-out mixtures it improves SI-SDR by +11.9 dB (a spectral gate: -3.9 dB), removes 17.9 dB where
there is handling noise and 0.15 dB elsewhere, and flags handling frames with F1 0.91. On a real held-out drop take
it flags exactly the five drops (precision 0.96, recall 1.0) and removes them by 27.8 dB. Details: the notebook,
`reports/handling-gpu/` and `reports/handling-poc/` (the smaller Mac-trained model).

## Proof-of-concept model (`kipml/`)
HandlingNet: a small STFT mask model (about 0.2M parameters) that removes phone-handling noise and
flags the frames where it happens. Training mixes handling clips into background sounds on the fly
at -5 to +20 dB, so there is no mixture set on disk. Python 3.12 via `uv` (`ml/pyproject.toml`).

| Command (run inside `ml/`) | Does |
|---|---|
| `uv run python -m kipml.train --steps 2000 --device cpu` | Trains (about 10 min on an M1 Pro CPU; `--device cuda` on the Lium pod). Writes `checkpoints/handling-poc.pt` |
| `uv run python -m kipml.evaluate` | Scores held-out mixtures against a spectral-gating baseline |
| `uv run python -m kipml.infer <any recording>` | **Test on a device's recording** (m4a, wav, ...): writes `<name>.clean.wav` and prints the flagged moments |
| `uv run python -m kipml.export` | Writes `models/handling-poc.onnx` and checks it matches PyTorch |
| `uv run --group dev pytest` | Unit tests |
| `uv run python -m kipml.report [--name handling-gpu --checkpoint checkpoints/handling-gpu.pt]` | Charts, numbers and before/after audio in `reports/<name>/` |

Labels: a frame is handling noise when the take is louder there than its own floor by 8 dB and, for our venue
takes, louder than the venue (90th percentile of the private room tone plus 3 dB). The training target keeps the
quiet parts of each take, so the model removes handling bursts and leaves the room alone.

Splits are by source file: `sleeve_03`, `pickup_01` and `pocket_02` from our takes, the last four
synthetic clips, ESC-50 fold 5 and the last 20% of each private recording are never trained on.

## Audio library
Every clip is 16 kHz mono 16-bit WAV. Licences and sources for every file: `audio/SOURCES.md`.

| Folder | What | Committed |
|---|---|---|
| `audio/ours/` | **Our recordings** from the demo iPhone: handling noise and room tone | yes |
| `audio/online/background/<category>/` | Night background sounds from ESC-50 (traffic, siren, construction, aircraft, rail, snoring, breathing, weather, room, footsteps). CC BY-NC 3.0 | yes |
| `audio/synthetic/handling/` | **Placeholder** procedural rustle, scrapes and bumps, with `labels.json` intervals, until real recordings exist | yes |
| `audio/generated/elevenlabs/` | Extra handling and background clips from ElevenLabs Sound Effects (once a key exists) | yes |
| `audio/private/` | Recordings with other people's conversation (venue room tone, Watch audio): training on the local machine or the Lium pod only | no |
| `audio/inbox/` | Drop folder for raw Voice Memos files | no |

## Add your recordings
1. Record on the demo iPhone with Voice Memos (Settings, Voice Memos, Audio Quality: Lossless).
   Background noise is fine; avoid nearby, clear conversation. At each spot record 1 to 2 minutes of
   room tone with the phone untouched, then 20 to 30 second takes of each kind of handling.
2. AirDrop the files to a Mac and name them `<spot>_<kind>_<nn>`: `corridor_sleeve_01.m4a`,
   `corridor_roomtone.m4a`. Kinds: sleeve, pocket, pillow, sheet, bedsheet, hoodie, jacket, pickup,
   bag, handling, roomtone.

======== models/README
# Models

Exported ONNX models the API loads, copied into the Docker image. `handling-v1.onnx` lands
here from the `ml` lane (#90). Raw data, runs and checkpoints stay out of git.

## handling-poc.onnx and handling-poc.pt (proof of concept)
`handling-poc.pt` is the same model as PyTorch weights (0.42M parameters, trained on a Lium RTX 3090), used by
`kipml.infer`, the notebook and any fine-tuning. The ONNX file is what the API runs.

Trained by `ml/kipml/` on our venue recordings, placeholders and ESC-50 (see `ml/README.md`). The
STFT stays outside the graph, so the server computes it (details in `handling-poc.json`):

- STFT: 16 kHz mono, n_fft 512, hop 160 (10 ms), Hann window 400 zero-padded to 512, centred.
- Input `features` [1, T, 257] = `log1p(10 * |STFT|)`.
- Output `mask` [1, T, 257]: multiply the complex STFT, then inverse STFT, for the cleaned clip.
- Output `logit` [1, T]: `sigmoid(logit) > 0.5` marks a 10 ms frame as handling noise.

`handling-v1.onnx` (#88) will take raw audio instead, with the STFT inside the graph.

import ExpoModulesCore

// Skeleton: the JS contract lives in ../index.ts. Real metering (AVAudioRecorder at 1 Hz, 10 s
// 16 kHz mono 16-bit WAV spike clips, SoundAnalysis speech check) is a later issue.
public class KipAudioModule: Module {
  private var recording = false

  public func definition() -> ModuleDefinition {
    Name("KipAudio")

    Events("onSample", "onSpike")

    AsyncFunction("start") { (options: StartOptions) in
      self.recording = true
    }

    AsyncFunction("stop") {
      self.recording = false
    }

    Function("isRecording") {
      return self.recording
    }

    AsyncFunction("deleteClip") { (uri: String) in
      // Later issue: delete the WAV at `uri`.
    }
  }
}

struct StartOptions: Record {
  @Field var spikeThresholdDb: Double = 0
}
======== Dockerfile
# One image, two processes: the API (default) and the worker
# (`bun apps/server/src/main.worker.ts`). The API also serves the Expo web build.
FROM oven/bun:1.4 AS install
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json bun.lock bunfig.toml ./
COPY apps/server/package.json apps/server/
COPY apps/mobile/package.json apps/mobile/
COPY packages/shared/package.json packages/shared/
RUN bun install --frozen-lockfile

FROM install AS web
COPY tsconfig.base.json ./
COPY packages/shared packages/shared
COPY apps/mobile apps/mobile
# Empty API URL: the web build calls the API on its own origin
ENV EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=""
RUN cd apps/mobile && CI=1 bun x expo export --platform web --output-dir dist

FROM oven/bun:1.4 AS server-deps
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json bun.lock bunfig.toml ./
COPY apps/server/package.json apps/server/
COPY apps/mobile/package.json apps/mobile/
COPY packages/shared/package.json packages/shared/
RUN bun install --frozen-lockfile --production --filter @kip/server

FROM oven/bun:1.4-slim
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production WEB_DIST=/app/web PORT=8080
COPY --from=server-deps /app/node_modules node_modules
COPY package.json tsconfig.base.json ./
COPY packages/shared packages/shared
COPY apps/server apps/server
COPY --from=web /app/apps/mobile/dist web
# The handling-noise filter the API loads (#90); ml/ itself stays out of the image
COPY ml/models ml/models
USER bun
EXPOSE 8080
CMD ["bun", "apps/server/src/main.api.ts"]

name: ci

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  checks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version-file: package.json
      - name: hq unit tests
        run: python -m unittest discover -s tools/hq/tests -v
      - name: Project setup (hq.json "setup")
        run: ./hq setup --ci
      - name: "Project checks (hq.json check: lint, typecheck, tests)"
        run: ./hq check

  terraform:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: infra
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: "~1.13"
          # The default wrapper breaks `terraform console` reading piped stdin
          terraform_wrapper: false
      - run: terraform fmt -check -diff
      - run: terraform init -backend=false -input=false
      - run: terraform validate
      - name: Render cloud-init with sample values and parse the YAML
        timeout-minutes: 2
        run: |
          python3 -m pip install --quiet pyyaml
          ./scripts/check-cloud-init.sh

  docker:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - name: Build the image (API, worker and web build)
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          push: false
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

# Kip: Devpost submission The text for Kip's Devpost page, one section per Devpost field. It was checked against `main` at commit `d18be9b` (2026-11-14). Anything not merged there is marked **planned**, with its issue or PR. Simulated data is labelled simulated, and the wording follows `docs/DOMAIN.md`. ## Before you submit (Ellis and Nick) Each item is still open. If only one, enter MongoDB Atlas (`docs/DECISIONS.md`). - [ ] **TODO:** Devpost does not render Mermaid. Export the diagram under "How we built it" as an image for the gallery. ## Project name Kip ## Elevator pitch Where in Newcastle would you sleep worst tonight? Kip links the city's night noise to sleep, street by street. ## About the project ### Inspiration Newcastle measures its night noise and people feel it, but nobody connects the two. The Urban Observatory publishes kerbside noise levels and the WHO publishes how night noise disturbs sleep, yet a resident can't tell what woke them, and a traveller can't tell that a hotel overlooks a 24-hour demolition site. Residents of Bewick Court were kept awake until 5am by demolition under a 24-hour permit, and no open dataset recorded it. ### What it does Kip shows how the city's noise is linked to sleep, street by street. Each part below says what works on `main` today and what is planned. **City sleep map.** Every Urban Observatory noise sensor, shaded by an indicative estimate of residents highly sleep disturbed, from its 30-night Lnight and the WHO road-traffic curve. The sensors sit at the kerb and the curve is for long-term road-traffic noise at a home's facade, so the map is an indicative road-traffic estimate, not a count of people kept awake. - Works today: the worker pulls Observatory noise, NO2 and PM2.5 every 5 minutes into Tiger Data. A continuous aggregate computes each sensor's nightly Lnight, and every 5 minutes Kip writes the 30-night Lnight and the indicative estimate onto each sensor in MongoDB, or "not enough data" below 30 nights. The web map renders Newcastle with Mapbox. - Planned: the 30-night backfill (#33), serving the sensors to the app (#35, open PR #128) and shading them on the map (#36). **Personal night.** Your night on one timeline: sleep stages from the Watch, bedroom noise in relative dB from the phone, and each wake-up linked to the spike it followed. Kip compares the wake-ups with 1,000 random moments from the same night and shows counts, such as "3 of 4 wake-ups followed a spike", because one night is too few for a percentage. It claims a link, never a cause. - Works today: the API stores an uploaded night (relative dB once a second, sleep stages and vitals in Tiger Data, a summary in MongoDB), keeping only the data types the upload has consent for. It counts the wake-ups that followed a spike against the random baseline. The Night tab draws the stages, the noise with its spikes, and the wake-ups. - Planned: recording on the phone while it is locked (#38, #59, #60), reading HealthKit (#39), uploading the night (#40), and wake-up marks on the timeline (#43, open PR #137). **Morning briefing.** A short spoken summary when you wake, such as "Two wake-ups followed drilling at 06:41, outside the council's recommended hours." - Works today, in the API: Kip gathers the night's facts (counts, labels and hours flags, never handling noise or levels), Gemini writes at most 40 words, and a guard rejects any draft that uses a phrase Kip must never say. After two rejected drafts Kip uses its own template. ElevenLabs then speaks the text. - Planned: the route that serves the briefing audio (#133; written, not yet mounted), the in-app player (#53) and playback on Apple Watch (#75, a stretch goal). **Live moment.** A drilling sound hits the phone, and within seconds Kip labels it, checks the council's recommended hours and briefs you. This is the centre of the demo. - Works today: the API takes the phone's levels once a second, finds spikes 10 relative dB above a 5-minute rolling median, checks each against Newcastle City Council's recommended hours for noisy work (Monday to Friday 08:00 to 18:00, Saturday 08:00 to 13:00, none on Sundays and bank holidays) and streams levels and spikes to the web dashboard. - Planned: the phone sending its levels (#57), and labelling live spikes with Gemini and briefing within seconds (#55). Until then a live spike arrives labelled `uncertain`. The demo's drilling clip will come from ElevenLabs Sound Effects (#58). **Quiet Stays.** Hotels ranked by how well you are likely to sleep there, for your profile: light sleeper, night out, best value or business. The Quiet Stay Score (0 to 100) is an indicative estimate of a hotel's surroundings, not of a room, with its sources one tap away. - Works today: the score's maths, profile weights and wording, and the ranking payload with example fixtures, in the shared package. The fixtures are simulated and flagged as simulated. - Planned: loading OpenStreetMap hotels and venues (#62), the MongoDB ranking pipeline (#63), the page with its profile switch (#64), and the roadworks search areas (#113, #115). Booking links are placeholders by design, because affiliate approval takes weeks. **Roadworks.** DfT Street Manager pushes street and road works permits over AWS SNS. - Works today: the SNS route checks each message's signature, confirms the subscription, stores Newcastle permits with their geometry in MongoDB, and finds the permits near a point whose dates overlap a stay. - Planned: a recorded sample of Newcastle permits (#67, in progress) and the works layer on the map (#68, #113). Live permits need the open data registration (#8) and a public HTTPS endpoint (#74). **Evidence log.** Planned: hash each night's log with SHA-256 and write the hash to Solana mainnet with the Memo program, then show a tamper check on stage (#71, #73, open PR #109). A memo proves when the log existed, not that the noise happened. Gemini will draft the out-of-hours report for the council (#72). **Privacy.** Sleep and heart data are special-category health data under UK GDPR. - Works today, in the API: consent per data type (microphone, HealthKit, location), a traveller profile, and one action that deletes everything a user has in both databases. Kip keeps no raw audio at rest. - Planned: the consent screens on first launch (#70, in progress), dropping clips with speech on the phone (#61), and deleting each clip once it is labelled (#44). **Our own model.** A phone on a nightstand or under a pillow hears itself: sleeves, pockets and bedsheets make spikes that would be labelled and linked to wake-ups. We trained a small model that finds and removes that handling noise. - Works today: a 0.42M-parameter mask model, trained in 14 minutes on a Lium RTX 3090 pod for $0.16, on our own venue recordings, ESC-50 night sounds and placeholder synthetic clips. On held-out mixtures it beats a spectral noise gate and flags handling frames with F1 0.91. On a real held-out phone take with five drops it flagged all five (precision 0.96, recall 1.0); other takes score lower (`ml/reports/handling-gpu/`). It is exported to ONNX, and a notebook shows the audio before and after. - Planned: the ONNX export with feature extraction inside the graph (#88, open PR #131), then running it in the API on each spike clip before Gemini (#90, #91). ### What is real, what is simulated | Data | Status | Where | |---|---|---| | Observatory noise, NO2 and PM2.5 | Real, pulled every 5 minutes from the Urban Observatory API | `apps/server/src/features/city/` | | City estimate per sensor | Real calculation; "not enough data" until a sensor has 30 nights (backfill: #33) | `sensor_lnight_daily` in Tiger Data | | Council hours and bank holidays | Real: Newcastle City Council's recommended hours, England bank holidays from gov.uk | `packages/shared/src/domain/` | | Night on the Night tab | **Simulated**, labelled "Simulated night." on screen, until a real night is uploaded (#49) | `apps/mobile/src/features/night/data/fixture.ts` | | Demo nights in tests | **Simulated** fixtures, which disagree on which wake-ups are linked (#135) | `packages/shared/src/night/fixtures/` | | Live dashboard | Real when the API is running. A development build that cannot reach the API plays a short **simulated** stream under a "Simulated stream" banner | `apps/mobile/src/features/live/` | | Labels on live spikes | `uncertain` until live labelling lands (#55). The "construction" label appears only in the simulated stream | | | Quiet Stays hotels and scores | **Simulated** fixtures, flagged `simulated: true`, with placeholder booking links | `packages/shared/src/stays/fixtures/` | | Street Manager permits | Real message format; tests replay recorded SNS messages. No live subscription yet | `apps/server/src/integrations/fixtures/street-manager/` | | Opted-in nights near hotels | Planned as a **simulated** cohort, always labelled simulated (#47) | | | Handling-noise training audio | Our own phone recordings, ESC-50 clips (CC BY-NC) and procedural placeholder clips | `ml/audio/` | | Demo drilling clip | Planned: generated with ElevenLabs Sound Effects (#58) | | ### How we built it ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph app["Kip app: one Expo codebase"] ios["iPhone
recorder and HealthKit"] web["Web dashboard
night, live view, map"] end subgraph sources["Open data"] obs["Urban Observatory"] sm["Street Manager
over SNS"] osm["OpenStreetMap"] end subgraph server["One Docker image"] api["API
Hono + tRPC"] worker["Worker
every 5 minutes"] end subgraph paid["Called only by the API"] gemini["Gemini
briefing text"] eleven["ElevenLabs
briefing voice"] solana["Solana Memo"] end model["Our handling-noise model
ONNX"] tiger[("Tiger Data
readings, Lnight aggregate,
night series")] mongo[("MongoDB
users, nights,
sensors, permits")] obs --> worker osm -.-> worker worker --> tiger worker --> mongo sm --> api web --> api ios -.-> api api --> tiger api --> mongo api --> gemini api --> eleven api -.-> solana api -.-> model classDef planned stroke-dasharray: 5 4 class ios,solana,model planned ``` Dashed: planned, not on `main` yet. - **Stack.** A Bun monorepo in TypeScript. One Expo (React Native) codebase builds the iPhone app and the web dashboard. The API is tRPC on Hono, and a node-cron worker runs from the same Docker image. Tiger Data (TimescaleDB) holds every timestamped value and MongoDB holds documents and geo queries. Terraform describes the Vultr server. - **The science is code.** The WHO curve, Lnight, the night window, construction hours, spike detection, the attribution maths, the score weights and the wording rules live in one shared package with tests, used by both the app and the server. - **Our model.** PyTorch, trained on a Lium GPU pod and exported to ONNX (`ml/`). - **Two people, parallel agents.** Ellis and Nick ran Claude Code and Cursor agents side by side: one GitHub issue, one branch and one PR each, coordinated by our `hq` CLI. The code is split by feature, so parallel agents rarely touch the same files. Entire recorded the sessions, gave each agent a Brain brief and Graph queries before it edited, and reviewed PRs with Claude Code and Codex. The agent framework was prepared before the event and is disclosed in the README. ### Challenges we ran into - **Sensors that are there, but quiet.** On the day, the only live Observatory Sound sensor sat 4.25 km from Grey's Monument, outside the 3 km circle the worker reads, and its series lagged the API clock by about an hour. The worker looks back 3 hours, and the 30-night backfill is next. - **A night that crosses the clocks.** Lnight is an energy average over 23:00 to 07:00 London time, including the nights the clocks change. TimescaleDB rejects a time bucket with both an offset and an origin, so the aggregate counts London days from a 07:00 origin instead. - **The phone hears itself.** Handling noise makes spikes that would be linked to wake-ups, so we trained our own filter. The `handling` label is never linked to a wake-up or spoken in a briefing. - **A loud venue.** Our recordings were full of other people talking. We scanned every take with Apple's sound classifier, cut the speech from committed clips and kept the rest out of git. - **Claims that survive judges.** One night has 2 to 6 wake-ups, the phone microphone is not calibrated, and the WHO curve is for road traffic at the facade. So Kip shows counts against a random baseline, relative dB and an indicative map, and its wording rules are code: a tested list of phrases Kip never says, which also screens every Gemini draft. ### Accomplishments that we're proud of - The science and the wording rules sit in one tested package that the app and the server share, so the claims on screen and in the briefing come from the same rules. - Our own model: trained for $0.16 of GPU time, it beats a spectral noise gate on held-out audio. - Two people and their agents built Kip in parallel, and every change reached `main` through a pull request with its agent session attached. ### What we learned - Writing the contracts first (the night upload schema, each payload with a fixture) let the app and the server start at the same time. - Wording rules are cheaper as code than as review comments. - Open data is only as live as its sensors: check what reports before building on it. ### What's next for Kip 1. Finish the live moment: phone streaming (#57), live labels and briefing (#55), and the briefing player (#53, #133). 2. A real night end to end: the recorder (#38, #59, #60, #61), HealthKit (#39), upload (#40) and clip labels (#44). 3. The city map: backfill (#33) and shading (#35, #36). 4. Quiet Stays (#62, #63, #64), the evidence log on Solana (#71, #73) and the deploy (#74). 5. The business: affiliate commission at launch, Verified Quiet in year one (hotels pay to replace the estimate with measured, room-by-room data), and area-level data licensing for councils and developers later. Renters choosing a flat may be a bigger market than hotel guests; that is a hypothesis, not a finding. ## Built with bun, typescript, react-native, expo, expo-router, tanstack-query, trpc, hono, zod, timescaledb, tiger-data, mongodb, gemini, elevenlabs, mapbox, maplibre, openstreetmap, urban-observatory, street-manager, aws-sns, pytorch, onnx, python, uv, lium, docker, caddy, terraform, vultr, github-actions, biome, entire, claude-code, cursor, codex ## Try it out - Code: https://github.com/ehewes/durhack-proj (private until the transcripts are reviewed; see the TODOs above) - Run it locally: `README.md`, "Run Kip locally" - **TODO:** live demo URL (#74) - **TODO:** backup video (#80) ## Prize tracks What each sponsor does in Kip today and what is planned. It claims a link, never a cause. - Works today: the API stores an uploaded night (relative dB once a second, sleep stages and vitals in Tiger Data, a summary in MongoDB), keeping only the data types the upload has consent for.
